title: AP Precalculus — Recap Set B (Unit 1 to 2.10)
question: Recap Set B: 13 questions in topic order from Unit 1 (rates of change, polynomials, rational functions, transformations, models) to 2.10 (sequences, exponential models, residuals, composition, inverses, logarithms); 9 calculations, 4 ideas.
intro:
**13 questions, Unit 1 to 2.10, in topic order.**

- 9 questions ask for a calculation: work it out on paper, then pick A–D.
- 4 questions ask for the idea behind a topic.
- The title of each question names the topic (1.2, 2.5, …).

**A calculator is allowed. Show your working before choosing A–D.**

questions.title: 1.2 · Average rate of change
questions.prompt: \(f(x) = 2x^2 + 1\). Find the average rate of change of \(f\) on \([0,\,3]\).
questions.solution_title: Change in output over change in input

questions.title: 1.3 · Rate of change from a table
questions.prompt:
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\\
\hline
f(x) & 20 & 17 & 12 & 5
\end{array}
\]

Which statement about \(f\) on this interval is true?
choices: \(f\) is decreasing and the graph is concave down
\(f\) is decreasing and the graph is concave up
\(f\) is increasing and the graph is concave down
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
17 - 20 &= -3 \\
12 - 17 &= -5 \\
5 - 12 &= -7
\end{aligned}
\]

- All differences negative: \(f\) is **decreasing**.
- The differences get more negative: the rate of change is decreasing, so **concave down**.
- Not linear: the differences are not all the same.

questions.title: 1.5 · Zeros and multiplicity
questions.prompt:
\[
p(x) = x^4 - 9x^2
\]

At which zero does the graph **touch the x-axis without crossing** it?
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
p(x) &= x^2\,(x^2 - 9) \\
&= x^2\,(x - 3)(x + 3)
\end{aligned}
\]

- \(x = 0\) has multiplicity \(2\) (even): the graph **touches** there. \(\boxed{x = 0}\)
- \(x = 3\) and \(x = -3\) have multiplicity \(1\): the graph crosses.
- \(x = 9\) is not a zero: \(p(9) \ne 0\).

questions.title: 1.10 · Holes
questions.prompt:
\[
r(x) = \frac{(x + 1)(x - 2)}{(x - 2)(x - 5)}
\]

Where does the graph of \(r\) have a **hole**?
questions.solution_title: A factor on top and bottom is a hole
questions.solution:
- \((x - 2)\) is a factor of both the top and the bottom: it cancels, leaving a **hole** at \(\boxed{x = 2}\).
- \((x - 5)\) stays in the bottom only: vertical asymptote at \(x = 5\).
- \((x + 1)\) stays on top only: zero at \(x = -1\).

questions.title: 1.12 · Transformations
questions.prompt:
The point \((3,\,5)\) is on the graph of \(f\). Let

\[
g(x) = -f(x + 2) - 4
\]

Which point is on the graph of \(g\)?
questions.solution_title: Inside moves x, outside moves y
questions.solution:
- \(x + 2\) inside: shift **left** by \(2\): \(x = 3 \to 1\).
- \(-(\dots) - 4\) outside: reflect over the x-axis, then down \(4\): \(y = 5 \to -5 - 4 = -9\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
g(1) &= -f(1 + 2) - 4 \\
&= -f(3) - 4 \\
&= -5 - 4 \\
&= \boxed{-9}
\end{aligned}
\]

- Not \((5, \dots)\): \(x + 2\) shifts left, not right.
- Not \((1, 1)\): the reflection makes \(5\) into \(-5\) before the \(-4\).

questions.title: 1.13 · Choose the model
questions.prompt:
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & 0 & 1 & 2 & 3\\
\hline
y & 3 & 10 & 17 & 24
\end{array}
\]

The \(x\) values go up by the same amount. Which type of function fits the data?
questions.solution_title: Equal steps in x, constant difference in y
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
10 - 3 &= 7 \\
17 - 10 &= 7 \\
24 - 17 &= 7
\end{aligned}
\]

- Each step **adds** the same \(7\): \(\boxed{\text{linear}}\), slope \(7\).
- Exponential would multiply by the same factor (\(10/3 \ne 17/10\)).

questions.title: 2.1 · Arithmetic sequence
questions.prompt: In an arithmetic sequence \(a_3 = 11\) and \(a_7 = 27\). Find \(a_{20}\).
questions.solution_title: Find d from the gap, then a_1

questions.title: 2.2 · Geometric sequence
questions.prompt: A geometric sequence has \(a_1 = 96\) and ratio \(r = \tfrac{1}{2}\). Find \(a_6\).

questions.title: 2.5 · Exponential model in context
questions.prompt: A car bought for \(€24{,}000\) **loses 15 % of its value every year**. About what is it worth after \(4\) years? (Calculator allowed.)

questions.title: 2.6 · Residual plot
questions.prompt:
A linear model is fitted to data. Reading the residual plot from left to right, the residuals are

\[
+,\ +,\ -,\ -,\ -,\ +,\ +
\]

What does this pattern tell you?
choices: The residuals add to about zero, so the linear model is a good fit
The residuals follow a curve, so a linear model is **not** appropriate
The data has no pattern, so no model fits
questions.solution:
- Positive, then negative, then positive: the data bends around the line, a **curved pattern**.
- A good model leaves residuals scattered randomly above and below zero.
- Summing to zero happens for every least-squares line, so it proves nothing.

\[
\boxed{\text{pattern} \Rightarrow \text{try a different model}}
\]

questions.title: 2.8 · Inverse functions
2.9 · Logarithmic expressions
questions.solution_title: Write both sides as powers of 2
questions.solution:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2^2)^{x} &= 2^5 \\
2^{2x} &= 2^5 \\
2x &= 5 \\
x &= \boxed{2.5}
\end{aligned}
\]

Check: \(4^{2.5} = 4^2 \cdot 4^{0.5} = 16 \cdot 2 = 32\).

- Not \(8\): that is \(32 \div 4\); a log asks for an exponent.
- Not \(3\): \(4^3 = 64\), too big.

questions.title: 2.10 · The logarithmic function
questions.prompt: \(f(x) = \log_2 x\). If the input \(x\) is **multiplied by 8**, what happens to the output \(f(x)\)?
questions.solution:
- \(\times 8\) is three doublings: \(8 = 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2\).
- Each doubling of the input adds \(1\) to \(\log_2 x\).

\[
\begin{aligned}
\log_2 (8x) &= \log_2 8 + \log_2 x \\
&= 3 + \log_2 x
\end{aligned}
\]

\[
\boxed{\text{output} + 3}
\]

- Check with \(x = 4\): \(\log_2 4 = 2\) and \(\log_2 32 = 5\). Up by \(3\).
- For an exponential it is the other way round: inputs add, outputs multiply.

takeaway: Unit 1 is about how functions change; Unit 2 is about functions that add (linear) or multiply (exponential), and running them backwards (logarithms).
